question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{1/2}3y{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{2}^{4}3y[{\int }_{0}^{1/2}{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}3y{[\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}]}_{0}^{1/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}3y(\frac{{e}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{e}^{0}}{4})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{3}{4}y({e}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{3}{4}y({e}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y & =\frac{3}{4}({e}^{2}-1){\int }_{2}^{4}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{3}{4}({e}^{2}-1)\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({e}^{2}-1)(\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}({e}^{2}-1)\end{aligned}
$$
